column1: # Where each gloss in lex-it.tsv was read.
# lemma | pos | tgt | sources | quote | stands
# The gloss is the English word an Italian word is woven for, and the tooltip
# prints it back: it is the claim every reader meets first. Every other
# claim the pack makes about a word names its entry — genders in
# it-genders.tsv, plurals in it-plurals.tsv, verb forms in it-verb-forms.tsv
# — and the gloss named none until 2026-10-08, the night fr-, es-, pt- and
# de-glosses.tsv were written the same way. Italian was the last of the five.
# Every row is read, all 356: the 178 nouns, 81 verbs, 57 adjectives, 22
# adverbs, 13 numerals and 5 interjections. Each was read in the rendered
# page of the word's English Wiktionary entry, in its Italian section: a
# script took the definition lines under each heading of the row's part of
# speech, examples, quotations and synonyms set aside, and drafted the first
# that holds the row's English word, and every quote was read against its
# page. Two drafts were another sense, and their lines quote the row's:
# luna's line holding "moon" is "(archaic, literary) a month, moon", and
# molto's first holding "very" is "much, very much, a lot (with verbs)",
# where the row's is the one before adjectives.
# A page holds every word of one spelling, so a quote is from this word's
# own part of speech where the page has it. Two rows' words have none of
# theirs, and their lines quote the heading the page gives them: primo,
# "first", is an ordinal adjective, and sì, "yes", a particle.
# The title is the word as Wiktionary's address writes it, with an
# underscore for a space: wikt:it:stare_in_piedi. A noun cites the entry its
# gender was read in, which for every Italian noun is its own. sedersi, a
# pronominal infinitive, defines itself, "to sit, sit down, take a seat",
# beside "reflexive of sedere", and needs no other entry.
# One phrase has no entry of its own: in nessun luogo, "nowhere". Its line
# cites the entries of its words, in, nessuno and luogo — nessun is
# "apocopic form of nessuno" — and quotes a line of each, joined by " / ",
# naming no stand-in; COMPOSED in tests/tools/glosses.test.ts lists it. Its
# variant da nessuna parte is an entry, "nowhere", and in nessun posto is
# not; teaching da nessuna parte instead is a call in TODO.md.
# Blank where the quote holds the row's English word. Otherwise it names the
# word of the quote that stands for it, because the English word is not in
# the entry, or is there only in another sense. Six rows need one. terra's
# entry is three lines, "ground", "soil" and "planet", so it is "soil" for
# "earth" and "ground" for "land"; tiepido for "warm" is "tepid, lukewarm",
# the entry that gives "warm" being caldo's, "warm, hot", which the pack
# weaves for "hot"; cercare for "seek" is "to look for"; salire for "rise"
# "to go up, to come up"; and luna for "moon" is "a natural satellite",
# Wiktionary filing the Moon itself under Luna.
# None is false. One says less than the row is woven for, and is recorded
# rather than changed: capello is "a single hair (on the head)", as French
# cheveu is one hair, where English's mass noun "hair" is capelli; see
# tests/tools/glosses.test.ts requires every row of lex-it.tsv to have a line
# here citing its own word's entry, whose quote holds its English word or the
# stand-in it names, and fails on a line outliving its row.
